title: 🎓 South Korea's Education Minister Resigns Over AI Cheating! A Hidden Camera and a Smartphone in the Exam Hall!
body: 🎓 South Korea's Education Minister Resigns Over AI Cheating! A Hidden Camera and a Smartphone in the Exam Hall!

South Korea's Education Minister Choi Kyu-jin resigned on Sunday, November 22, and President Lee Jae Myung accepted his resignation within about an hour, after widespread criticism of how the ministry handled the threat of AI cheating ahead of the national university entrance exam, the country's most important exam.

The crisis began four days before the exam, when the top scorer in the certified tax accountant exam admitted he had cheated using a miniature hidden camera and a smartphone that sent photos of the questions to an AI service to generate the answers, earning him a near-perfect score.

The ministry acted late and kept changing its measures until the last moments: after first focusing on smart glasses, it rushed out new measures including sticking stickers on clothing buttons to block hidden cameras, tightening glasses inspections, limiting permitted writing tools to black pencils only, blocking public Wi-Fi networks around exam centers, and sending emergency alerts to phones across the country three times during the exam to expose phones their owners had not handed in.

The measures led to 111 suspected cases of cheating with electronic devices being caught on exam day, with about half of them uncovered thanks to the emergency alerts. The controversy grew when the minister was asked in parliament three days before the exam whether he was confident of catching every case of AI cheating, and he answered that he did not think so "because of his age" — he is 72 — which was seen as dodging responsibility.

After accepting the resignation, the president wrote that concerns about AI cheating extend from the entrance exam to university essay entrance exams and school tests, that exam fairness is a principle that cannot be compromised, and ordered a review of plans to add identification marks to question papers so their source can be traced if they are photographed or leaked.

Simply put: a small camera and a smartphone brought down a minister, because AI cheating now threatens the fairness of Korea's most important exam — can any monitoring system keep up with new cheating technologies?
Do you think AI has made cheating in exams easier? And how can schools confront it?
